title: S'mores Icebox Cake with Toasted Meringue
changes_from_base: A no-bake loaf of graham crackers brushed with coffee, layered with chocolate mousse and whipped cream, then covered in blowtorched Italian meringue, instead of sponge and ice cream.
summary: A towering frozen take on the campfire classic, with silky chocolate mousse, cream and coffee-soaked crackers finished under a cloud of toasted meringue.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm rimmed baking tray lined with foil
23 x 33 cm rimmed baking tray lined with foil

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
large egg whites (about 140 g), at room temperature

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: Melt 198 g dark chocolate with 180 ml double cream over barely simmering water, stirring occasionally for about 10 min, then whisk smooth off the heat and stir in the 3 egg yolks once the mixture is just warm.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the 3 egg whites with ¼ tsp salt and the optional espresso powder until foamy, then stream in 50 g caster sugar and whisk to glossy medium-stiff peaks, about 8 min.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Fold a quarter of the meringue into the chocolate mixture to loosen it, then fold in the rest and chill the mousse.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whip 240 ml double cream with 15 g caster sugar and ⅛ tsp salt to medium-stiff peaks, about 2 min.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Line the loaf tin with cling film and build up layers of graham crackers brushed with 60 ml coffee, chocolate mousse and whipped cream, repeating to use four cracker layers and finishing with crackers brushed with coffee.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and chill for at least 6 h, then turn the cake out onto a foil-lined tray, peel away the cling film and freeze for about 1 h until firm enough to slice.

steps.title: Meringue
steps.text: Whisk 4 egg whites on low speed while boiling 200 g caster sugar with 120 ml water to 115 °C, then whisk the whites to soft peaks, pour in the hot syrup down the side of the bowl and whisk on high until stiff and no longer warm, about 10 min.

steps.title: Torch
steps.text: Swoosh the Italian meringue over the top of the cake and brown it with a kitchen blowtorch held 3-5 cm away.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Cut into 8 portions with a hot, dried knife.

tips: Pour the 115 °C sugar syrup down the side of the bowl rather than onto the whisk, then whisk on high until stiff and no longer warm, so the meringue is glossy and holds its swooshes under the blowtorch.
Use pasteurised eggs for the mousse and meringue if serving pregnant women, young children, older people or anyone unwell, since neither fully reaches 71 °C.
Keep the blowtorch moving steadily over the meringue so it browns evenly without scorching.
Dip the slicing knife in hot water and dry it between cuts for neat, clean slices.
storage: The cake can be frozen without its meringue for up to 1 week; add and torch the meringue just before serving.
